solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Broadcast media getting behind most of fool's tirade

indicators.note: to get behind is to follow, so the scrambled word comes after the shortened fool
most of a word means all but its final letter is kept

parts.note: a jerk is a fool

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sounds off at the media for latching on to a fool's rant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' rearranges the media letters into EMIAD; 'getting behind' and 'most of' are the other indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeremiad is a long, mournful complaint or denunciation, a kind of tirade.

clue.text: Left work cuddled by flier in car

indicators.note: the bird holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a jay is a bird, a flier
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone left the job to snuggle up with a pilot in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalopy is an old, battered motor vehicle.

clue.text: Desert island's brought in only so much to eat

indicators.note: the island letter is introduced into the phrasal verb

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert or betray them
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: On a desert island, food has been brought in but just enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert island' reads as one phrase, but 'Desert' gives RAT ON and 'island' I.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed allowance of food, a limited portion.

clue.text: Run from blue deer

indicators.note: the run letter is taken away from the mood word

parts.note: blue means gloomy, morose
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A gloomy deer runs off.
explanation.definitionFit: A moose is the largest kind of deer, called an elk in Europe.

clue.text: A vote against including Labour's first street researcher

indicators.note: the vote word takes in the initial letter

parts.note: a nay is a vote against

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A street researcher counts a no vote that includes Labour's top candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyst examines data closely to find patterns, a kind of investigator.

clue.text: House cracked externally — something of a comedown

indicators.note: the word for cracked sits on the outside, wrapping the abbreviation for house

parts.note: cracked means crazy, bats

explanation.surface: A house cracked on the outside is a bit of a letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is an anticlimax: a sudden drop from the elevated to the trivial, a comedown in tone.

clue.text: I garble badly in account of some mathematics

indicators.note: the anagram goes inside the abbreviation for account
done badly, the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to mangling the account of some sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles GARBLE into LGEBRA; with I after it, that goes 'in' AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebraic means relating to algebra, a branch of mathematics using symbols.

clue.text: One seeking early Asian lock

parts.note: the Huns were an ancient nomadic people from Central Asia
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone searches for a lock of an ancient Asian's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A huntress is a female hunter, someone pursuing game.

clue.text: Still name carried by tin soldier?

indicators.note: the symbol for tin holds the label word within

parts.note: SN is the chemical symbol for tin
a tag is a name or label
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A toy soldier made of tin wearing a name tag stays still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin soldier' looks like a toy figure, but the two words work separately; the question mark admits the stretch of soldier for a kind of ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is still, not flowing.

clue.text: Came in to land leading to tense examination of the shore

indicators.note: one piece comes before the next in the answer

parts.note: a bird lit (alighted) when it came in to land
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A bird coming in to land precedes a tense examination of the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Littoral is an adjective for things relating to or situated on a coastline.

clue.text: Range around last items for discussion

indicators.note: the cooker name goes round the word for finish

parts.note: an AGA is a British brand of cast-iron kitchen range cooker
the last part of something is its end

explanation.surface: Looking at a range of the last things on a list to talk about.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a heavy British range cooker, so 'Range' gives AGA, not a spread of values.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of matters to be taken up at a meeting.

clue.text: Have some weight and box, disposing of unknown

indicators.note: getting rid of the algebra letter

parts.note: the box is British slang for television, the telly
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Boxers make weight, discarding anything unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' is the TV set, British TELLY, not boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell means to count or have effect, as in the strain began to tell.

clue.text: In pursuit of power, see Tory confused about Liberal convert

indicators.note: the following material comes after the power letter

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the Liberal abbreviation
confused letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A power-hungry Tory, muddled, defects from the Liberals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' makes ROSEYTE, which 'about' wraps round L; 'In pursuit of' puts it after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A proselyte is a new recruit to a faith or cause, someone who has been converted.

clue.text: Destined to inhale oxygen or another element

indicators.note: breathing in takes the gas symbol into the middle of the word

parts.note: born to do something means destined for it
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Something fated to take in oxygen, or else a different element.
explanation.definitionFit: Boron is a chemical element, number 5, so a different one from oxygen.

clue.text: Kick that a gambler wants?

definitions.meaning: in rugby, a kick of the ball dropped from the hands

explanation.surface: A gambler craves a thrill, a kick.
explanation.definitionFit: Punt is both a rugby kick from the hands and British slang for a wager.

clue.text: Man is knocked out in middle of wild excitement — stars seen here?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit within the trimmed word
only the middle of the word for uproar is used, losing its outer letters

parts.note: a furore is a wild outburst of excitement

indicators.note: letters knocked out of shape are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is floored amid wild excitement, seeing stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked out' scrambles MAN IS into SAMIN, put 'in' UROR, the middle of FURORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Minor, the Little Bear, is a constellation, a group of stars in the sky.

clue.text: Affair is going ahead after one lands in US city

indicators.note: the pieces are joined in order with the city coming first
the numeral arrives inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
I is the Roman numeral one
something going ahead is on

explanation.surface: An affair is under way now that someone has touched down in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic or sexual relationship, an affair.

clue.text: Evidence of wound? I'm the very thing involved — a sword

indicators.note: the mark wraps round the other pieces, involving them

parts.note: a scar shows where a wound was
I'm without its apostrophe is IM
it means the very thing, the ideal

explanation.surface: A scar declares that it was caused by a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved oriental sabre.

clue.text: Spice mother concealed in cannon

indicators.note: the parent word is hidden inside the shot word

parts.note: in billiards a cannon is a carom, hitting two balls in one shot
a dam is a mother animal

explanation.surface: Mother has hidden spice in a cannon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cannon' is the billiards shot CAROM, not a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardamom is an aromatic seed used as a spice in curries and baking.

clue.text: Church, unaltered, containing second structure

indicators.note: the phrase for unaltered holds the letter for second

parts.note: as is means left unchanged

explanation.surface: A church left untouched has a second building inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the base frame or structure of a vehicle or appliance.

clue.text: Send spades with it

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
hip and with it both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: Dispatch the spades along with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ship goods is to send or dispatch them.

clue.text: Avoid love

definitions.meaning: to ... a question is to dodge it
love is zero in tennis; zero in cricket, and in Britain both are casual endearments

explanation.definitionFit: Duck means dodge, and it is a British pet name like love, as well as a zero score.

clue.text: Sowed lines in parched surroundings

indicators.note: the lines are put into the dry word
the dry word forms the surroundings of the lines

parts.note: parched means dried

explanation.surface: Seeds planted in rows in dry ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To drill seed is to sow it in furrows made by a seed drill.

clue.text: Hard stone split by instant cut

indicators.note: the stone abbreviation is parted by the shortened word

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight

indicators.note: cut means trimmed of its last letter

parts.note: in a trice means in an instant

explanation.surface: A hard stone splits in an instant when cut.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is stone, the British unit of 14 pounds; 'cut' trims TRICE to TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict means severe or harsh, as in a strict regime.

clue.text: Succeeded getting groom to get a move on?

parts.note: to curry a horse is to groom it with a currycomb

explanation.surface: A successful groom is told to hurry up.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry is to hurry along with quick little steps.

clue.text: Number of lines in program ultimately repeated in bit of IT kit

indicators.note: the poem sits between the two copies of the final letter
the chosen letter is used twice
ultimately points to the final letter of the word program

parts.note: a number is a piece of verse; an ode is a poem, a number of lines

explanation.surface: Counting lines of code in a program on a computer device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a count but means a poem (an ODE). 'ultimately' picks M, 'repeated' doubles it, and the ode goes 'in' between.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem is a device that links a computer to a phone or cable line, a piece of IT hardware.

clue.text: Stupid to keep mum regarding one variety of language

indicators.note: the adjective holds the word for mother inside it

parts.note: stupid means idiotic
ma is a word for mum

explanation.surface: It's daft to stay quiet about a variety of language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like silence but is a mother, MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic describes expressions natural to a particular language or dialect, its native usage.

clue.text: Satisfied aluminium will suffice for this?

definitions.text: Satisfied aluminium will suffice for this?

parts.note: met a demand means satisfied it
AL is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Aluminium will do the job well enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: aluminium is one example that would satisfy this category.
explanation.definitionFit: Aluminium is a light silvery element of the class of conducting materials it exemplifies.

clue.text: Tango? Current male popular, having good co-ordination

parts.note: T is Tango in the NATO alphabet
I is the physics symbol for electric current
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A popular man dancing the tango has good coordination.
explanation.definitionFit: Timing is the skill of coordinating actions at the right moment, as dancers and athletes need.

clue.text: Woman's following fool about Independent's arbiter of fashion?

indicators.note: the woman's word comes after the fool

parts.note: a clot is a fool, British slang

indicators.note: the pronoun goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a woman's thing is hers; her is the possessive

explanation.surface: A woman trails after a fool around the Independent newspaper's fashion pundit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a clothier sells clothes rather than judges style.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothier makes or sells garments, so in a playful sense decides what people wear.

clue.text: Note gospel is linked to studies in religion

indicators.note: the two pieces are joined side by side

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject
Mark is one of the four Gospels

explanation.surface: A note says the Gospel ties in with religious studies.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is a school subject in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Remark and note can both mean to observe or comment on something.

clue.text: I really make an effort to curb the French form of worship

indicators.note: the phrase hems in the French article

parts.note: I do try is an emphatic way of saying I really make an effort
la is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone insists they try hard to rein in French-style worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is the worship of idols or images, one kind of religious devotion.
